newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi delegation off to Ankara for talks on cordon.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi delegation off to Ankara for talks on cordon.

text.p: An Iraqi delegation is on its way to Ankara to express Baghdad's opposition to Turkish plans to set up a security zone in northern Iraq, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said on Monday.

"The delegation, including a number of specialists, will hold talks with the Turkish side on bilateral relations and will in particular inform the Turkish government of Iraq's firm and clear stand on the latest decision Turkey has been talking about, which pertains to the so-called security zone in Iraqi territory," INA said.
INA said the delegation was headed by Hamed Youssef Hummadi, a former information minister and currently a presidential adviser.
Turkey has announced plans for a security cordon in northern Iraq up to 10 km (six miles) deep to prevent infiltration by Turkey's Kurdish guerrillas fighting for autonomy from Ankara.
Washington said it would not object but the plan has drawn condemnation from Iraq and criticism from many other countries of the region.
Iraq last week summoned Turkey's acting charge d'affaires in Baghdad to complain about Ankara's plans. An Iraqi official on Sunday warned of unspecified measures if Turkey proceeded.
